bug_description.normalized: The staged 32768-byte witness reaches `fuzz_parse_http_request()`, which truncates `length` to the 32767-byte global `data_copy` buffer and copies only the first 32767 bytes. That copied prefix still contains `\r\n\r\n` at offsets 32762..32765 so `read_request_finalizer()` admits the request, and `identify_http_path()` accepts the oversized request line ending at `HTTP/1.0\r` on offset 32756. In `parse_headers()`, the truncated logical span ends at `buffer_end = data_copy + 32767`; after two ordinary header-scan iterations the loop reaches `p == next_chr == data_copy + 32766`, the lone trailing `\r` left behind when truncation drops the original final byte `0x69`. The vulnerable empty-line check tests only `next_chr == next_hdr`, so it enters `STRING_SWITCH_SMALL(next_hdr)` without the remaining-length predicate added by the patch. `STRING_SWITCH_SMALL` expands to `string_as_int16(next_hdr)`, and `memcpy(&i, s, sizeof(int16_t))` reads bytes 32766 and 32767, so the second byte is one past global `data_copy`. AddressSanitizer reports `global-buffer-overflow READ 2` at `string_as_int16`. The patch fixes this exact obligation by changing the branch to `if (next_chr == next_hdr && buffer_end - next_chr > 2)`.

source.description: First project-side consumption of the attacker input. This clamp converts the 32768-byte witness into the truncated logical request length `32767` that all later parser bounds derive from, so the copied request ends on a lone trailing `\r` at offset 32766.
source.value_from: The staged file `gt_results/arvo_14511/poc` is exactly 32768 bytes (sha256 `c46f6ce5d8a5bc2db2dd5eedc1e788bd76208c20e733ac0e4f0dd9f67d43c567`). On entry to `fuzz_parse_http_request()` that makes `length > sizeof(data_copy) == 32767`, so this statement clamps the logical request extent to 32767 before the subsequent copy and all downstream `buffer_end` calculations.

sink.description: ASan crash site. `s` equals `next_hdr = data_copy + 32766`, so this 2-byte copy reads the last valid `\r` and then byte 32767, one byte past the end of global `data_copy`.

root_cause.description: Incomplete blank-line guard. The branch treats any `\r` at the current scan position as an empty header line and immediately performs a two-byte lookahead, but it never checks the remaining logical span against `buffer_end`. The patch adds the missing predicate `buffer_end - next_chr > 2` at this exact line.

tainted_value_origin.description: The first concrete vulnerability-relevant state is the truncated request length. The 32768-byte witness is clamped to `sizeof(data_copy) == 32767`, so parsing uses only the first 32767 bytes and the published buffer ends with a lone `\r` at offset 32766 instead of the original trailing byte `0x69`.

parser_admitted.description: Within the truncated 32767-byte prefix, `has_crlfcrlf()` finds `\r\n\r\n` at offsets 32762..32765, so the finalizer accepts the witness and `fuzz_parse_http_request()` proceeds to `parse_http_request()`. The same copied prefix also contains `HTTP/1.0\r` at offset 32756, letting request-line parsing reach `parse_headers()`.
parser_admitted.condition: The first 32767 copied bytes preserve an internal `\r\n\r\n` terminator before the final lone `\r`.

coarse_trace.summary: The fuzz helper truncates the 32768-byte witness to the 32767-byte global `data_copy`, publishes that `(value,len)` pair to the parser, and the saved finalizer/request-line checks admit the request.
`parse_http_request()` accepts the oversized `GET ... HTTP/1.0` request line inside the truncated buffer and dispatches the remaining suffix to `parse_headers()`.

The header scanner reaches the lone trailing `\r` at the last copied byte, and the missing remaining-length check on the `next_chr == next_hdr` branch allows a two-byte `STRING_SWITCH_SMALL` lookahead on that one-byte suffix.
The two-byte `memcpy()` in `string_as_int16(next_hdr)` reads one byte past the end of global `data_copy`, producing the saved AddressSanitizer global-buffer-overflow read.

fine_trace.note: The staged witness is 32768 bytes, so the fuzz helper clamps `length` to 32767 before any parsing. This singular truncation drops byte 32767 (`0x69`) and makes the logical request end on the preceding `\r` at offset 32766.

Copies the truncated 32767-byte prefix into global `data_copy`. The copied tail is `30 0d 6c 22 6c 22 0d 0d 0a 0d 0a 0d`, so `data_copy[32766] == '\r'` and the following byte belongs to the ASan redzone, not the request.

Publishes the copied bytes to the parser as the logical request span `[data_copy, data_copy + 32767)`. All later bounds decisions in `read_request_finalizer()`, `identify_http_path()`, and `parse_headers()` use this truncated `(value,len)` pair.

Inside `parse_headers()`, the vulnerable parser materializes the logical end pointer `buffer_end = data_copy + 32767`. This is the boundary the patch later uses in the missing guard `buffer_end - next_chr > 2`.

After `parse_http_request()` has accepted the request line ending in `HTTP/1.0\r` at offset 32756 and two ordinary loop iterations advanced `p` through `(32758,32761)` and `(32763,32764)`, this search runs with `p == 32766` and returns `next_hdr = data_copy + 32766`, the lone trailing `\r` at the last valid byte.

Root cause. Because `next_chr` and `next_hdr` are both `data_copy + 32766`, this empty-line branch is taken on a single trailing `\r`. The branch condition checks only equality and omits the remaining-length predicate `buffer_end - next_chr > 2` added by the patch, so the subsequent two-byte lookahead executes even though no second in-bounds byte exists.

Sink. `STRING_SWITCH_SMALL(next_hdr)` expands to `string_as_int16(next_hdr)`, so `s` is `data_copy + 32766`. This `memcpy()` reads bytes 32766 and 32767; byte 32767 is one past global `data_copy`, producing the saved `AddressSanitizer: global-buffer-overflow READ 2`.

poc.trigger: The saved Stage 01 command runs `request_fuzzer` on this exact file and reproduces `AddressSanitizer: global-buffer-overflow READ 2` in `string_as_int16()`, with stack `parse_headers -> parse_http_request -> fuzz_parse_http_request`.

format.name: truncated oversized HTTP/1.0 request ending in a lone carriage return
format.contract: Exactly the 32768-byte witness stored in `poc` (sha256 `c46f6ce5d8a5bc2db2dd5eedc1e788bd76208c20e733ac0e4f0dd9f67d43c567`). The fuzz helper truncates it to the first 32767 bytes before parsing. In that copied prefix, the request line ends with `HTTP/1.0\r` at offset 32756, `\r\n\r\n` appears at offsets 32762..32765 so the finalizer admits the input, and the copied buffer ends with a lone `\r` at offset 32766 because byte 32767 (`0x69`) is dropped. Those exact witness properties are the verified trigger for the missing `buffer_end - next_chr > 2` guard in `parse_headers()`.
